notes: Page image p.139 (Table 1, Mohs scale) confirms iron nail = 4.5 and apatite 5, feldspar 6, quartz 7, topaz 8, corundum 9, diamond 10: six minerals are harder than 4.5, so key 6 is correct and unique. The text also states that a harder mineral scratches a softer one (fluorite 4 scratches calcite 3 but not apatite 5). The explanation, including the distractor count of 4, is correct. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against the lesson (المعادن - جواهر الأرض, hardness) and it fits. The Arabic is correct.

The page image (p.91, section الأجهزة) calls a group of organs that work together to do one function a الجهاز, and gives the stomach, mouth, intestines and liver working together in digestion as the example. That matches display key 3 (الجهاز). The distractors are the other levels of organization on the same page (cell, tissue, organ) and each is clearly wrong. The explanation is correct and matches the source. The stem stays close to the textbook wording, which fits a difficulty-1 definition item. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against the lesson's organization levels and it fits. The Arabic is correct.

The page image p.165 (continuing from p.164) says secondary waves travel in solids only and move rock particles at right angles to their direction of motion. It also says primary waves are the fastest, travel in solids, liquids and gases, and compress the rock in their direction of motion, and that surface waves are the slowest and travel only on the surface. So display key 2 (الأمواج الثانوية) is the one defensible answer. The explanation matches the source. Its rationale for the 'all three' distractor is a little contrived but not wrong. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against the lesson's seismic-evidence section and it fits. Difficulty 2 and the Arabic are fine.

issues.span: فصل العلب الفلزية عن بقية النفايات في مصنع لإعادة التدوير باستخدام مغناطيس كبير
issues.suggestion: The page says only some metals (بعض الفلزات) are attracted to a magnet, and aluminium cans are not. Use 'فصل العلب الحديدية (الفولاذية)' so the scenario does not imply that every metal can is magnetic.

notes: The page image p.89 supports all four pairs. Malleability is the ability to be hammered into thin sheets, which makes copper suitable for art. Ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires, and copper wires are used for wiring in buildings. Luster comes from the surface reflecting light. Some metals are attracted to magnets (Fig. 8 shows a crane magnet). The blind answer matches key_display exactly. Melting point is a valid unused distractor. The wires scenario mentions conducting electricity, but conductivity is not an option, so the pairing is not ambiguous. The explanation is correct and uses 'بعض الفلزات' correctly. The scenarios closely mirror the textbook examples, so difficulty is closer to 2 than the stated 3. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against the lesson and it fits. The Arabic is correct.

Blind answer matches key (display 1). p23 (image) states heated air expands, becomes less dense, rises and gives low pressure while colder denser air gives high pressure; p25 (image) states air moves from high to low pressure and describes the India monsoon (low pressure over land -> moist wind from ocean), which the explanation cites correctly. The sea breeze itself is not named in the pages, so the item is a transfer application; the stem supplies the land-heats-faster premise and 'near the surface' rules out option 3 (p26's hot-air-toward-poles statement concerns global circulation). Distractors map to real misconceptions. Estimated difficulty 3 vs stated 4 (one-step transfer of an explicitly taught rule); within tolerance. Arabic is correct. Objective field is null in the packet, so objective alignment was judged against the lesson (atmosphere and weather: pressure and wind), which it fits.

issues.suggestion: Set difficulty to 2: every example in all four options is named verbatim on pp.92-94 with its classification (rust, browning apple, burning wood, tarnished silver on p92; caramel, electrolysis, salad in blender, baking cake on p93; melted butter, clay flower on p94), and each distractor contains exactly one clearly physical change, so the item is recognition of textbook examples rather than a level-4 reasoning task.

notes: Blind answer matches key (display 0). Images read for pp.92-94: p92 lists iron gate rusting, peeled apple/banana browning in air, burning wood producing ash and silver losing its shine as chemical changes; p93 lists heating sugar to caramel and electrolysis of water as chemical, whipping salad in a blender as not chemical, and baking cake (gas bubbles) as chemical; p94 gives melting butter and shaping clay as reversible physical changes. Each distractor therefore has exactly one physical member (salad, butter, clay) and the key has none; exactly one defensible answer. Explanation is correct and consistent with the pages. Arabic is correct and uses the textbook terms. Objective is null in the packet; alignment judged against the lesson (chemical properties and changes), which it fits. The only issue is that stated difficulty 4 (which alone makes it high-risk) is too high.

Blind answer (false, display 1) matches key. p68 image states directly that Figure 24 shows carnivore teeth are more wedge-shaped than herbivore teeth, carnivore teeth cut and tear meat while herbivores grind plant matter; the figure captions say predator teeth are wedge-shaped for tearing and herbivore teeth are flat for grinding. The item reverses that comparison, so 'false' is the single defensible answer. Explanation's wedge definition (moving inclined plane with one or two sloping faces) and the cut/grind contrast match the page. Difficulty 2 is appropriate for a reversed-statement recall item. Arabic is correct and uses the textbook terms (الإسفين، مفلطحة، الطحن). Objective is null in the packet; alignment judged against the lesson (work and simple machines, the wedge), which it fits.

All data needed is in the stem; integer answer with zero tolerance and optional unit is unambiguous. Explanation is correct and its reversed-division misconception (0.625) is a sensible note. Difficulty 2 fits a single-step proportional computation. Arabic is correct; the stem uses Western digits while the textbook uses Arabic-Indic digits, which is a display convention rather than an error. Objective is null in the packet; alignment judged against the lesson (scientific models, map scale application), which it fits.

Explanation is consistent with the page; 'تجوية ميكانيكية' is supported by the page context. Objective is null; item fits the lesson on weathering.

Page images confirm each pairing: Mercury closest/smallest with craters (p51), Mars two moons and iron-oxide red sediments (p52), Uranus horizontal rotation axis (p53), comet of ice and rock with bright tail near the Sun (p54), meteorites as rock/metal pieces falling to Earth with some aged 4.5 billion years (p54, printed '٤,٥'). Both distractors (Jupiter, asteroid belt) are correct descriptions of bodies not listed, so no second defensible match. Explanation consistent with source. Direct recall with distinctive descriptors; difficulty closer to 2 than 3. Objective null; fits lesson.

Page images: p187 wind deposits and migrates sand dunes (Fig. 26); p188 river slows at sea and deposits a delta; p186 glaciers widen valleys into a U shape (Fig. 25); p185 rockslide detaches rock layers and piles large rock pieces at the slope base, listed as a mass movement, with Fig. 24 caption naming gravity as the downslope pull. The gravity link for rockslides is implicit rather than stated in one sentence on the cited pages (the explicit statement is probably on p184), but gravity is the only option that fits. Chemical weathering is a sound distractor. Explanation correct. Objective null; fits lesson.

The Dead Sea example in the explanation is on the page. The stem's east/west variant of the textbook's north/south example is valid. The phrase 'دون أن تتباعدا أو تتقاربا' rules out all three distractors, so the item is on the easy side (about 2). Objective null; fits lesson.

Blind answer matches key (display 0). Page 165 image confirms the text layer: the sun is the main energy source, green plants use solar energy to make food, and animals get energy by eating plants or eating animals that eat plants. The figure caption also asks why most ecosystems cannot survive without sunlight. The key follows directly from that chain. The distractors are clearly wrong per the page (only plants make food; water is not supplied by sunlight; carnivores still depend on sunlight). The explanation is correct and consistent with the source. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against lesson n3363 (abiotic factor: sunlight), which the item practises. Difficulty 4 is slightly high for one two-link chain the page states outright; 3 fits better. Arabic is correct and uses curriculum terms.

All four blind pairs match key_display. Page 170 image confirms the text layer. It defines predation (one animal feeds on another; example: a falcon takes a field mouse), mutual benefit (both benefit), commensalism (one benefits and the other neither benefits nor is harmed; example: nests in trees) and parasitism (one benefits and the other is harmed; example: insects on zebra skin causing disease). Each scenario is a direct analogue of one of these. Competition works as a distractor that fits none, and the explanation says so. The explanation is correct and uses the page's definitions. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against lesson n3364 (relationships in communities). Each scenario states who benefits and who is harmed, so difficulty 3 is slightly high; 2 fits better. Arabic is correct.

Blind answer matches key (display 1). Page 143 image confirms the text layer. Platypus females have no nipples; the mammary glands secrete milk onto the mother's skin or fur and the young lick it directly. The distractors map to page facts: the nipples inside a pouch belong to marsupials (Fig. 17), and option 0 contradicts the stem's own premise that milk is involved. The umbilical-cord point in the explanation is not on this page, but it is correct and consistent with the curriculum. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against lesson n3356 (types of mammals). The item is close to direct recall of a stated fact, so difficulty 3 is slightly high; 2 fits better. Arabic is correct and uses curriculum terms (الثدييات الأولية، الغدد اللبنية).

issues.suggestion: Some bacteria make their own food, including cyanobacteria and the nitrifying bacteria that live in home aquaria. Name the bacteria's role in the stem, e.g. 'وبكتيريا تتغذى على الفضلات وبقايا المخلوقات الميتة', so that 'البكتيريا' is unambiguously a decomposer as p.172 presents it.
The page gives bacteria as an example of decomposers ('المحللات كالبكتيريا والفطريات'), not all bacteria. Write 'والبكتيريا في الحوض محلِّلات تتغذى على الفضلات…' instead of a general claim.

notes: Blind answer matches key (display 0). The page images confirm the text layers. On p.171, green algae are food for snails and fish and supply oxygen through photosynthesis. On p.172, producers make their own food by photosynthesis, and decomposers such as bacteria and fungi feed on waste and remains. On p.175, producers make their own food and consumers feed on other organisms. Within the curriculum's framing the key is the only answer. A strong student might contest the bacteria distractor, hence ambiguity minor and verdict warn. Pages 173-174 are cited in the range but not needed. Objective is null, so alignment was judged against lesson n3364 (producers, consumers, decomposers). Difficulty 1 is appropriate. Arabic is correct and uses curriculum terms.

A one-step percentage for grade 7 reads closer to difficulty 2 than 3; not blocking. High-risk (numeric/computation): evidence-extractor overlap still required.

Explanation correct and consistent with the source. Difficulty 2 appropriate.
